title: Barangay Solid Waste Management Crisis
description: Your barangay has been experiencing severe localized flooding during the rainy season. The Barangay Council discovered that the primary cause is the heavy accumulation of single-use plastics and household garbage in the local esteros (creeks) and drainage canals. The community lacks discipline in segregating waste, and garbage trucks often fail to collect on time due to narrow streets.
context: Solid waste management is a persistent issue at the barangay level under R.A. 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000). The barangay is mandated to handle the collection of biodegradable and recyclable wastes, while the city/municipality handles residual wastes.
constraints: Propose an information campaign that targets households to practice proper waste segregation at the source.
Design a low-cost, community-led monitoring system to prevent illegal dumping of garbage in the esteros.
Outline a logistical plan for waste collection that accommodates the narrow streets of the barangay.

issues: Improper Waste Disposal in Waterways
Lack of Household Waste Segregation
Weak Policy & Enforcement by Tanods
Irregular Collection in Narrow Alleys

causes.title: Limited Budget for Garbage Collection
causes.description: Inadequate funds to hire extra trucks for narrow interior alleys.

causes.title: Poor Enforcement of Waste Regulations
causes.description: Barangay Tanods rarely fine violators or monitor esteros at night.

causes.title: Rapid Urban Population Growth
causes.description: Increased household density generating more daily garbage.

causes.title: Improper Household Segregation
causes.description: Residents mix biodegradable, recyclable, and hazardous waste together.

causes.title: Lack of Civic Awareness
causes.description: Residents do not recognize long-term flooding risks of illegal dumping.

evidenceLibrary.title: Government Solid Waste Compliance Report
evidenceLibrary.snippet: Official LGU audit showing Barangay waste collection efficiency is at 45% with zero segregation compliance.
evidenceLibrary.fullText: The 2025 Municipal Environment and Natural Resources Office (MENRO) report highlights that 55% of estero blockages stem from unsegregated household plastic bags. Recommends strict enforcement of RA 9003.

evidenceLibrary.title: Estero Clean-up Photo & Drainage Survey
evidenceLibrary.snippet: High-resolution photos documenting severe plastic bottleneck accumulation at the Main Bridge canal.
evidenceLibrary.fullText: Photographic documentation from the City Engineering Office shows over 3 tons of plastic debris clogging the culvert entrance during July heavy rains.

evidenceLibrary.title: Community Resident Satisfaction Survey
evidenceLibrary.snippet: Survey of 200 households indicating 78% complain about irregular garbage truck arrival schedules.
evidenceLibrary.fullText: A random sampling survey conducted by local SK volunteers found 78% of residents dump garbage at corners because municipal collection trucks skip narrow interior streets.

evidenceLibrary.title: Barangay Annual Budget Report
evidenceLibrary.snippet: Financial statement showing 12% allocation for environmental sanitation and solid waste management.
evidenceLibrary.fullText: The 2025 Barangay Budget allocated ₱250,000 for waste management. However, ₱180,000 was spent on truck fuel, leaving minimal funds for educational campaigns or eco-bricks.

evidenceLibrary.title: Local News Feature Story
evidenceLibrary.snippet: Regional news coverage of urban flooding in low-lying barangays.
evidenceLibrary.fullText: Channel 7 special report: 'Flooding in Sector 4 intensifies as plastic waste chokes urban waterways despite municipal clean-up drives.'

evidenceLibrary.title: Social Media Community Group Post
evidenceLibrary.snippet: Viral Facebook post by a resident complaining about foul odor and blaming neighboring barangays.
evidenceLibrary.fullText: Post with 1.2k shares: 'The garbage here is intolerable! Why are people from nearby barangays throwing their trash in our estero at midnight?! Officials do nothing!'

evidenceLibrary.title: Sanitation Officer Interview Transcript
evidenceLibrary.snippet: Interview with Head Barangay Health Worker detailing increased vector-borne diseases near waste sites.
evidenceLibrary.fullText: Dr. Santos: 'Accumulated moist trash near esteros has caused a 30% surge in localized skin infections and mosquito breeding in Sitio Riverside.'

evidenceLibrary.title: Barangay Topographic & Waterway Map
evidenceLibrary.snippet: GIS mapping highlighting flood vulnerability zones and current garbage collection routes.
evidenceLibrary.fullText: Spatial map demonstrating that 4 out of 6 Sitio alleys are inaccessible to standard 6-wheeler municipal garbage trucks.

stakeholders.name: Aling Rosa
stakeholders.initialStatement: The garbage truck rarely comes into our narrow alley. If we don't dump our trash by the creek, flies swarm inside our small house!

followUps.question: Would your family segregate waste if the barangay provided color-coded bins or collection schedules?
followUps.answer: Yes, definitely! Most of us want a clean street, but we need clear collection times so trash isn't left on the pavement all day.

followUps.question: Are residents willing to participate in a weekend sitio clean-up drive?
followUps.answer: If the Barangay Captain leads it and provides gloves and trash bags, many mothers and youth here will gladly volunteer.

stakeholders.name: Captain Manuel Cruz
stakeholders.initialStatement: We have limited funds for new mini-dump trucks, but we enforce local ordinances when Tanods catch illegal dumpers at night.

followUps.question: Can the Barangay Council authorize partnerships with local junk shops for recyclables?
followUps.answer: That is a great idea! Selling segregated plastics and metals directly to accredited junk shops can fund our BDRRM environmental project.

followUps.question: Why are Tanods struggling to stop midnight dumping?
followUps.answer: We only have 8 Tanods covering 5 Sitios. Without CCTV or community volunteers, we cannot monitor every corner 24/7.

stakeholders.name: Engr. Mark Torres
stakeholders.initialStatement: Republic Act 9003 mandates barangays to handle segregation and composting. Municipal trucks only collect non-recyclable residual waste.

followUps.question: How can the Municipality assist our barangay with narrow alley collection?
followUps.answer: We can deploy push-carts (pedicabs) or 3-wheeler Eco-Bikes to shuttle waste from inner alleys to the main highway transfer station.

unexpectedEvent.title: Unexpected Challenge: Municipal Waste Budget Reduction
unexpectedEvent.description: Due to emergency calamity fund reallocations, the Municipal Government has cut barangay waste subsidies by 30%. Fuel for heavy collection trucks will be reduced next month.

options.text: Reduce activities and cancel all information campaigns.
options.feedback: Canceling information campaigns stops civic education, leading to worse long-term waste accumulation.

options.text: Mobilize SK youth volunteers to construct community Eco-Pads and partner with local recycling junk shops for self-funded waste collection.
options.feedback: Excellent adaptive decision! Community-led recycling creates a sustainable revenue stream and fosters local ownership.

options.text: Request an immediate emergency loan from the provincial government.
options.feedback: Emergency loans require lengthy legislative approval and do not address root cause sustainability.

options.text: Increase mandatory fines on households by 200%.
options.feedback: Drastic fines without providing collection infrastructure causes resentment and increases illegal midnight dumping.

stepTips.1: Read carefully. Differentiate symptoms from root issues before prioritizing.
stepTips.2: Analyze cause relationships. Consider which factor triggers the others.
stepTips.3: Balance your evidence library. Combine official reports with community experiences.
stepTips.4: Gather diverse perspectives. Interview both local leaders and grassroots residents.
stepTips.5: Ensure your intervention plan is evidence-based, actionable, and sustainable.
stepTips.6: Anticipate real-world constraints. Adapt your plan without sacrificing core objectives.
stepTips.7: Assess ethical implications. Make sure vulnerable groups are protected and benefit.

title: Dengue Outbreak Prevention
description: During the onset of the rainy season, the local health center reported a significant spike in Dengue fever cases within your barangay, particularly affecting children. Health workers identified multiple empty lots and neglected areas acting as breeding grounds for mosquitoes due to stagnant water.
context: Barangays play a crucial role in preventative healthcare. The DOH advocates the '4S Strategy' against Dengue: Search and destroy mosquito-breeding sites, Self-protection measures, Seek early consultation, and Support fogging/spraying only in hotspot areas.
constraints: Formulate a community-wide 'Search and Destroy' clean-up drive schedule involving local youth (SK) and community volunteers.
Create a strategy to compel owners of abandoned or empty lots to clear their properties of stagnant water.
Propose an educational initiative to teach children and parents about self-protection measures using locally available resources.

issues: Unattended Stagnant Water in Abandoned Lots
Low Community Participation in Search & Destroy
Delayed Medical Consultation by Affected Families
Lack of Insect Repellent & Self-Protection Access

causes.title: Insufficient Public Health Education
causes.description: Families misunderstand early dengue symptoms, confusing them with simple fever.

causes.title: Irregular Household Water Storage
causes.description: Uncovered water drums (drum/tanke) stored inside homes due to water interruptions.

causes.title: Neglected Private Abandoned Lots
causes.description: Absentee property owners leave containers that accumulate rain water.

causes.title: Dense Neighborhood Vegetation
causes.description: Overgrown weeds and uncleaned gutters providing mosquito resting spots.

evidenceLibrary.title: Barangay Health Center Epidemiological Surveillance Report
evidenceLibrary.snippet: 42 confirmed dengue cases recorded in Sitio 2 and Sitio 4 within the last 30 days.
evidenceLibrary.fullText: City Health Office report indicates a 140% spike in pediatric dengue admissions. High mosquito larval index discovered in stagnant puddles in Sitio 2.

evidenceLibrary.title: DOH 4S Strategy Policy Circular
evidenceLibrary.snippet: Department of Health guidance emphasizing 4pm daily Search & Destroy drives.
evidenceLibrary.fullText: Official DOH protocol highlights that eliminating breeding containers is 10 times more effective than chemical fogging alone.

evidenceLibrary.title: Sitio Abandoned Lot Aerial & Photo Inspection
evidenceLibrary.snippet: Photo log showing 12 discarded tires filled with rainwater in fenced empty lot.
evidenceLibrary.fullText: Inspection team photos confirm abandoned rubber tires are functioning as primary mosquito breeding hotspots.

evidenceLibrary.title: Parent Survey on Mosquito Repellent Usage
evidenceLibrary.snippet: Survey showing 65% of families cannot afford daily commercial lotion repellents.
evidenceLibrary.fullText: Local BHW survey reveals financial hardship prevents low-income households from buying commercial repellents.

followUps.question: What is your main concern?
followUps.answer: We want clear guidelines and assistance.

followUps.question: What is your main concern?
followUps.answer: We want clear guidelines and assistance.

unexpectedEvent.title: Unexpected Challenge: Chemical Fogging Supply Shortage
unexpectedEvent.description: The City Health Office ran out of chemical fogging solution due to high regional demand. How will your team adapt?

options.text: Cancel all anti-dengue activities until chemical supplies arrive.
options.feedback: Canceling activities allows mosquito larvae to hatch unchecked.

options.text: Double down on manual 'Search and Destroy' clean-up drives and distribute neem-oil natural repellents.
options.feedback: Outstanding decision! Manual container destruction is the most effective biological control.

stepTips.1: Identify root breeding environments vs individual infection symptoms.
stepTips.2: Analyze how stagnant water storage triggers mosquito population spikes.
stepTips.3: Use official epidemiological reports alongside parent survey evidence.
stepTips.4: Consult municipal health officers and local barangay health workers.
stepTips.5: Design actionable 'Search and Destroy' routines for households.
stepTips.6: Focus on sustainable physical clean-ups when chemical fogging is unavailable.
stepTips.7: Ensure vulnerable children and low-income families receive free protection.

title: Stray Animal Population and Rabies Threat
description: There has been an alarming increase in the number of stray dogs and cats roaming the barangay streets. Several residents, including a young student, were recently bitten by a stray dog. The barangay currently has no local animal pound and limited funds for mass vaccination.
context: The Anti-Rabies Act of 2007 (R.A. 9482) requires LGUs to control stray animals, while barangays are tasked with assisting in the registration and vaccination of dogs, as well as conducting information campaigns on responsible pet ownership.
constraints: Develop a campaign promoting responsible pet ownership, specifically targeting the registration and confinement of pets within household premises.
Propose a partnership or collaboration strategy with local NGOs or the City Veterinary Office to conduct a low-cost mass anti-rabies vaccination drive.
Design a humane reporting and response system for aggressive stray animals within the barangay.

issues: Unvaccinated Free-Roaming Stray Dogs
Irresponsible Pet Ownership & Unconfined Animals
Lack of Local Barangay Animal Pound Facility
High Cost of Post-Bite Anti-Rabies Vaccines

causes.title: Uncontrolled Animal Breeding
causes.description: Pet owners do not spay/neuter pets, leading to unwanted litters.

causes.title: Lack of Fenced Yards
causes.description: Low-income households allow pets to roam streets freely during daytime.

causes.title: Inadequate City Vet Outreach
causes.description: Mass vaccination drives happen only once every two years.

evidenceLibrary.title: City Veterinary Rabies Audit Report
evidenceLibrary.snippet: Rabies vaccination coverage in Barangay is at 38%, well below the 70% herd immunity target.
evidenceLibrary.fullText: City Vet audit confirms 62% of domestic dogs remain unvaccinated against rabies, posing severe public health risks.

evidenceLibrary.title: Barangay Health Center Animal Bite Incident Log
evidenceLibrary.snippet: 14 bite incidents reported in past 2 months near elementary school.
evidenceLibrary.fullText: Bite log shows 10 out of 14 bites involved unconfined stray dogs during school dismissal hours.

stakeholders.name: Dr. Fernando Garcia
stakeholders.initialStatement: We can provide free rabies vaccine vials if the barangay organizes pet registration and volunteer vaccinators.

followUps.question: Can the City Vet help conduct low-cost spay and neuter clinics?
followUps.answer: Yes! We partner with Humane Society NGOs to provide free spay/neuter for registered low-income pets.

unexpectedEvent.title: Unexpected Challenge: Vaccine Transport Delay
unexpectedEvent.description: Free vaccine cold-chain transport from the regional office has been delayed by 2 weeks. How will you proceed?

options.text: Cancel registration drive and pet owner seminars.
options.feedback: Canceling delays community awareness and pet leash enforcement.

options.text: Proceed with household pet registration, census, and leash enforcement while queueing pets for arrival.
options.feedback: Excellent choice! Preparing the census ensures 100% vaccination efficiency when vaccines arrive.

stepTips.1: Focus on vaccination rates and responsible pet ownership constraints.
stepTips.2: Trace uncontrolled breeding and unconfined roaming causes.
stepTips.3: Review City Vet audit logs alongside bite incident records.
stepTips.4: Engage veterinary experts and local pet owner associations.
stepTips.5: Build a humane registration and vaccination action plan.
stepTips.6: Maintain momentum with registration census when supplies are delayed.
stepTips.7: Protect both human safety and animal welfare ethically.

title: Youth Engagement and Curfew Implementation
description: The Barangay Tanods have reported an increase in incidents involving youth loitering late at night, leading to noise complaints, vandalism, and minor altercations. The Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) has a budget but struggles to create programs that genuinely interest the local youth.
context: Under the Local Government Code, the barangay enforces local ordinances including curfews for minors, while the SK is mandated to promulgate resolutions necessary to carry out programs for youth development.
constraints: Design an engaging, non-traditional recreational or skill-building program funded by the SK to keep the youth productive during evenings or weekends.
Propose a restorative justice approach (rather than punitive) for first-time curfew violators apprehended by the Barangay Tanods.
Create a communication plan to inform parents of their responsibilities regarding the barangay curfew ordinance.

issues: Youth Nighttime Loitering & Noise Complaints
Lack of Productive Evening Recreational Programs
Friction Between Tanods and Out-of-School Youth
Inadequate Parental Guidance & Curfew Awareness

causes.title: Lack of Evening Youth Spaces
causes.description: Barangay plaza lights are turned off at 8 PM, leaving street corners as only hangout spots.

causes.title: Boredom & Out-of-School Youth Idle Time
causes.description: Few athletic, digital, or vocational programs available past school hours.

causes.title: Punitive Enforcement Friction
causes.description: Tanods approach youth confrontationally rather than mentorship-focused.

evidenceLibrary.title: Barangay Peace & Order Incident Blotter
evidenceLibrary.snippet: 28 noise blotters involving minors logged between 10 PM and 2 AM.
evidenceLibrary.fullText: Blotter entries confirm majority of incidents involve loud music and street tambayan altercations near Sitio 3 store.

evidenceLibrary.title: SK Youth Needs Assessment Survey
evidenceLibrary.snippet: 84% of surveyed youth requested night basketball leagues and e-sports/coding workshops.
evidenceLibrary.fullText: Survey reveals youth want structured sports leagues, music jams, and IT skill workshops during weekends.

stakeholders.name: Hon. Patricia Cruz
stakeholders.initialStatement: We have ₱150,000 in our SK fund ready to support evening sports, arts, and vocational training programs.

followUps.question: Can SK organize a weekend night sports league under court lights?
followUps.answer: Yes! We can sponsor floodlights, referees, and team jerseys to keep youth active in positive sports.

unexpectedEvent.title: Unexpected Challenge: Covered Court Maintenance Closure
unexpectedEvent.description: The main barangay covered court will be closed for roof repairs for 3 weeks. How will you adapt youth programs?

options.text: Cancel all youth activities until court reopens.
options.feedback: Canceling activities leads youth back to unmonitored late-night street corners.

options.text: Pivot to indoor e-sports, chess tournaments, and acoustic music jams at the Barangay Hall Multi-Purpose Room.
options.feedback: Great adaptation! Utilizing indoor facilities keeps youth engaged without needing the covered court.

stepTips.1: Differentiate constructive youth activities from punitive curfew enforcement.
stepTips.2: Analyze underlying causes of youth boredom and idle evening hours.
stepTips.3: Cross-reference blotter logs with youth survey requests.
stepTips.4: Collaborate with SK leaders and community youth representatives.
stepTips.5: Design restorative justice and skill-building programs.
stepTips.6: Pivot smoothly when sports venues are undergoing repairs.
stepTips.7: Foster youth empowerment and positive community integration.

title: Barangay Disaster Risk Reduction (BDRRM) Preparedness
description: Your barangay is situated near a river and is highly susceptible to flooding during typhoons. However, the community lacks a clear early warning system, and residents often refuse to evacuate until the floodwaters have already reached dangerous levels.
context: R.A. 10121 (Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act) requires every barangay to have a functioning BDRRM Committee and an updated community-based disaster risk reduction and management plan.
constraints: Design a localized, easy-to-understand Early Warning System (EWS) that can reach all residents, including those without smartphones or internet access.
Formulate a plan to organize and train a community-based volunteer rescue and relief team.
Propose an intervention strategy to convince hesitant residents to undergo pre-emptive evacuation before a typhoon strikes.

issues: Hesitation & Delay in Pre-Emptive Evacuation
Inaccessible Early Warning Signals for Non-Smartphone Users
Lack of Trained Community Volunteer Rescuers
Inadequate Facilities at Flood Evacuation Centers

causes.title: Fear of Property Theft During Evacuation
causes.description: Heads of households stay behind to guard belongings against looters.

causes.title: Sirens Not Audible in Interior Sitios
causes.description: Barangay megaphone warning system does not reach narrow riverbank alleys.

causes.title: Lack of Color-Coded Flood Level Markers
causes.description: Residents cannot visually gauge when river water is reaching critical flood heights.

evidenceLibrary.title: MDRRMO River Inundation & Flood Risk Map
evidenceLibrary.snippet: Riverbank Sitios 1 and 5 reach 1.5-meter flood depth within 45 minutes of heavy rain.
evidenceLibrary.fullText: Hydrological audit confirms flash floods inundate low-lying riverbank homes rapidly during Signal No. 2 storms.

evidenceLibrary.title: Evacuation Center Capacity & Needs Assessment
evidenceLibrary.snippet: Elementary school evacuation center can shelter 80 families with modular tents.
evidenceLibrary.fullText: Assessment shows evacuation center has adequate sanitation and modular privacy tents for pre-emptive evacuees.

stakeholders.name: Mr. Danilo Reyes
stakeholders.initialStatement: Pre-emptive evacuation saves lives. We need color-coded sirens and trained neighborhood captains.

followUps.question: How can we assure residents their homes will be guarded while they are in the evacuation center?
followUps.answer: We deploy dedicated Tanod Security Patrols and static checkpoints in evacuated Sitios.

unexpectedEvent.title: Unexpected Challenge: Sudden Power Outage & Cell Network Loss
unexpectedEvent.description: A severe typhoon knocked out electricity and cellular towers across the barangay. How will you issue early warnings?

options.text: Wait for power and mobile network signal to be restored.
options.feedback: Waiting for power during a flood emergency leads to casualties.

options.text: Deploy hand-crank sirens, color-coded flags, and house-to-house megaphone Tanod teams.
options.feedback: Outstanding emergency decision! Low-tech physical warning systems save lives when power fails.

stepTips.1: Prioritize early warning reach and pre-emptive evacuation readiness.
stepTips.2: Examine why residents hesitate to leave homes during typhoons.
stepTips.3: Analyze flood inundation maps alongside evacuation facility audits.
stepTips.4: Consult BDRRM officers and neighborhood Sitio leaders.
stepTips.5: Formulate a multi-channel Early Warning System (sirens, megaphones, flags).
stepTips.6: Use physical low-tech warning tools when power and internet fail.
stepTips.7: Ensure elderly, children, and vulnerable families are safely evacuated first.
